trend.title: KBRA: CMBS Delinquency Rate Rises to 7.7% in September, Led by Office and Multifamily
trend.scope: KBRA-rated U.S. private label CMBS universe ($344.4 billion)
trend.metric: 30+ day delinquency rate up 9 bps to 7.7%
trend.summary: KBRA's September 2026 CMBS Loan Performance Trends report found the 30+ day delinquency rate among its rated U.S. private label CMBS universe rose 9 basis points to 7.7% in September from 7.6% in August, while the distress rate (delinquent plus current-but-specially-serviced loans) fell 4 bps to 10.3%. Loans totaling $1.6 billion were newly added to the distress rate, and 74.9% of that newly distressed balance ($1.2 billion) involved imminent or actual maturity default rather than a performance default. The office sector accounted for the largest share of newly distressed loans (47.7%, $757.5 million), followed by multifamily (14.6%, $231.5 million) and mixed-use (13.6%, $216 million).
trend.significance: A newly distressed pool running nearly three-quarters maturity defaults, rather than cash-flow defaults, signals that more borrowers are reaching their loan's maturity date unable to refinance or sell -- the direct precursor to the foreclosure, receivership, and workout litigation this tracker follows. The office and multifamily concentration in this month's new distress points to where that litigation is most likely to surface first over Q4.
